name: Janet Louise Harwood
public: My propensity is 4, because I like the idea of a ready-to-drink gazpacho as a convenient, vegetable-forward option — it fits my habit of keeping prepared soups on hand for low-energy days and I enjoy mild, savory breakfasts and lunches. I would buy it provided the bottle lists a low-sodium recipe, isn't overly spicy, and is reasonably priced (or from a local maker I trust). It's especially appealing in warmer months or as a light lunch with whole-grain crackers. If it were very high in salt or the flavor too sharp, I'd be less likely to repurchase, but I would certainly try it once.

name: Stephen Michael Donnelly
public:
Hello — I’m Stephen Michael Donnelly, 68, a senior research technician and part-time independent research consultant based in San Francisco. I work with community clinics and neighborhood health projects; I teach practical lab procedures, help with small-scale assay workflows, and do volunteer outreach through my parish.

Top 10 interests (in rough order):
1) Community health projects and neighborhood screenings
2) Cooking hearty vegetarian meals (stews, dals, soups)
3) Reading approachable science and public-health writing
4) Gardening on my small balcony (herbs, tomatoes)
5) Translating technical results into plain language for community partners
6) Tinkering with small repairs and inexpensive lab instruments
7) Attending quiet local talks or lectures on health policy
8) Listening to folk/acoustic and older singer-songwriter music while I cook
9) Light console gaming (puzzle/strategy games) for short sessions
10) Following curated public-health discussions on social media and newsletters

Gazpacho question: My propensity is 2. Very unlikely but not impossible. Reason: I value home-cooked soups and stews that I can reheat and control for ingredients; I’m skeptical of processed convenience items with long ingredient lists or preservatives. A bottled cold soup would only tempt me in hot weather if it came from a trusted local maker, had a short, recognisable ingredient list (tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, olive oil, vinegar, salt), and was reasonably priced. Otherwise I’d prefer to make my own or buy from a deli that makes it fresh.

name: Warren Ellis Gentry
public: My propensity is 2 — very unlikely, but not impossible. First, I'm a country fella who prefers warm, slow-cooked dishes and home-made staples; cold blended soup isn't part of my regular meals. Second, when I want something like that I'd sooner make a pitcher from garden tomatoes or buy it from a local vendor I trust than reach for a bottled product with mystery ingredients. Third, I might try a bottle once in the heat of summer out of curiosity, especially if it's local and the label is honest about ingredients and price, but I wouldn't buy it regularly. So: 2.

name: Evan McAllister
public: My propensity is 3, because I'd maybe buy ready-to-drink gazpacho but it depends. I like fresh veg-forward food and would try it on a hot day or when I'm short on time, especially if it's from a local maker, bottled in glass, reasonably priced, and tastes like real tomatoes/peppers (not overly sweet or canned). I usually prefer to make things at home, and Noah probably wouldn't eat it, so it wouldn't be a regular family staple — more of an occasional convenience or summer treat. If the flavor profile included a little heat or tang, that'd increase the chances.

name: Rosa María Castañeda
public:
My name is Rosa María Castañeda. I'm 59, work nights as a CNA at a small long-term care facility in Milwaukee, and live with my husband Carlos. My daughter Mimi helps with online things and my little granddaughter Sofia is my joy. I keep life simple: I like familiar, home-cooked food and steady routines.

Top-10 interests (short list):
1) Simple traditional home-cooked meals (stews, arroz con pollo, tamales)
2) Short, family-style novels and saga stories in Spanish/English
3) Regional Mexican ballads and soft Christian music
4) Mending clothes / simple sewing and embroidery
5) Quiet church activities (rosary groups, potlucks)
6) Small domestic rituals (coffee, window light, balcony herbs)
7) Neighborhood and parish community events / festivals
8) Bargain hunting and practical shopping for essentials
9) Quiet evening walks when my back allows
10) Family photos and keeping family recipes

About the gazpacho question: My propensity is 2 (very unlikely). Why: I prefer hot, familiar dishes and simple snacks I know how to trust; a bottled cold Spanish soup feels a bit unfamiliar and like a novelty to me. I worry about price, preservatives, and portion size. I might try one small bottle if it were cheap or Mimi recommended it on a hot day, but I probably would not buy it regularly. Mira, that’s honest — convenient could win me over sometimes, but not often.

name: Erin Michelle Dalton
public:
Hello — Iu0002m Erin Michelle Dalton. Iu0002m 44 and work as an administrative coordinator at a small community health clinic in Portland, Oregon. I try to be practical about food and prefer simple, healthful meals.

Top 10 interests (brief):
1) Reading long-form nonfiction about public health and policy
2) Cooking simple, Mediterranean-leaning meals
3) Travel to historic cities with relaxed itineraries
4) Following a few public-health and regional-news podcasts
5) Small music shows and mellow singer-songwriters
6) Volunteering for clinic outreach and food drives
7) Neighborhood association involvement and town-hall meetings
8) Serialized investigative journalism and supporting nonprofit outlets
9) Gentle home-improvement and decluttering projects
10) Balcony herb gardening (basil, thyme, mint)

About the gazpacho question: My propensity is 3, because while the flavors (tomato, cucumber, olive oil, lemon) line up well with what I like and it would be appealing in warmer months, Iu0002m cautious about ready-to-drink bottles. I would want a clear ingredient list, modest sodium, and reasonable price. If itu0002s sold refrigerated, clearly labeled, and priced like a light lunch or substantial snack, Iu0002d consider buying it occasionally (especially in summer). Iu0002m not an automatic buyer of novel packaged foods, so Iu0002d say u0002maybeu0002 — open to trying if the packaging and price look honest.

name: Anthony James Holloway
public: My propensity is 3 — maybe I'd buy it. Here's why: I ain't against trying new, convenient foods, and a chilled gazpacho sounds all right on a hot day, but it's not the kind of filling, meat-centered thing my family usually eats. If y'all put it in a small, inexpensive bottle (say under a few dollars), labeled plainly with simple ingredients and sold chilled in the supermarket, I'd pick one up now and then for myself as a refreshing snack. I wouldn't buy it for a family dinner or as a regular staple unless the price and portion made sense. Things that'd make me more likely: a sampler, a sale, or a familiar brand doing a mild-flavored version. Things that'd make me less likely: high price, fancy packaging that makes it seem expensive, or a flavor that's too vinegary or spicy. Hope that helps — I can also give y'all my self-intro and top-10 interests if you still need that.

name: Marjorie Keating
public:
Hello — this is Marjorie Keating. I’m 76 and I work a couple mornings a week as a part-time library assistant at our neighborhood Boston branch. I’m happy to be honest and helpful. A quick note on my interests, in case it helps your research: 1) Knitting and simple crafts (I teach a basic pattern at the library sometimes). 2) Listening to public radio (NPR) with my morning tea. 3) Small church activities and the monthly potluck. 4) Reading large-print mysteries and local-history pieces. 5) Gentle, older folk and country music; humming along while shelving CDs. 6) Simple home cooking and family recipes (baked chicken, casseroles, apple pie). 7) Gardening — my little back-patio geranium and herbs. 8) Small day trips to nearby seaside towns or a local museum. 9) Volunteering at the library and helping with neighborhood drives. 10) Baking a casserole or a small treat to bring to neighbors or the staff room.

Now, about the bottled ready-to-drink gazpacho: My propensity is 3 — maybe I would buy it, not sure. Because: I’m cautious about new food products and I watch my salt, so I’d only try it if the flavor sounded mild and the label said low-sodium and simple ingredients. I’d be more likely to buy one in warm weather as a small, refreshing treat, especially if it was a single-serving bottle and I could sample it first or a neighbor recommended it. If it tasted too acidic, raw, or spicy, or if it was pricey for the size, I’d pass. In short — possible in summer under the right conditions, otherwise unlikely.
